title: AI-CE: AI Cost Estimation
description: AI cost estimation from CAD drawings: parsing, detection, and structured models.
image_alt: AI cost estimation from CAD drawings
subtitle: End-to-end AI-assisted cost estimation system integrated with a CAD application: data, models, backend, database, CAD add-on, and UI.
overview: AI-CE is an end-to-end AI-assisted cost estimation system integrated with a CAD application. It was built from the ground up, covering data exploration, AI model development, information extraction, backend services, database integration, CAD add-on development, and the user interface. A user submits CAD-related input from the CAD application; the backend runs preprocessing and AI inference and returns structured results to the CAD add-on, where the extracted information is reviewed and used in the estimation workflow. Project data and processing results are stored in MySQL.
problem: Manual interpretation of CAD and project information for cost estimation needs repeated review and data entry.
Objective: a usable end-to-end workflow rather than a standalone ML experiment, connecting drawing-based input to automated information extraction and estimation-related outputs.
Keep the CAD application as the user-facing client and run processing and inference on the server.
contributions: Designed and developed the system from the initial concept through end-to-end integration.
Built the data analysis, model experimentation (YOLO, DETR), and information-extraction components.
Developed the Python backend (FastAPI) and connected it to the CAD-side functionality.
Developed the CAD add-on / UI integration, the MySQL and Redis data workflows, and the Prometheus/Grafana monitoring.

process.title: Requirements and workflow design
items: Defined the input expected from the CAD application and the output needed by the estimation workflow.
Planned responsibilities across CAD add-on, backend, AI models, and database.
Mapped the full request–response path from CAD to server and back.

process.title: Data collection, exploration, and analysis
items: Collected and examined project and drawing-related data.
EDA to understand format, variation, quality, and edge cases.
Identified preprocessing and annotation requirements.

process.title: Preprocessing and model-ready dataset
items: Transformed input data into a format suitable for training and inference.
Prepared training/validation data and checked quality.
OpenCV for image-processing operations.

process.title: AI model development and experiments
items: Object-detection components with Python, PyTorch, and YOLO.
DETR tested as an alternative architecture (experiment, not the deployed model).
Iterated on training, validation, and behaviour across representative inputs.

process.title: Information extraction and result structuring
items: Transformed AI outputs into structured information for the backend and CAD add-on.
Downstream processing to turn predictions into estimation-related data.
Consistent response format for CAD integration.

process.title: Backend API and server-side inference
items: Backend services with Python and FastAPI.
CAD submits input; the server runs processing and inference and returns results.
Redis integrated as part of the backend stack.

process.title: Database and data management
items: MySQL for project data and application/inference records.
Backend read/write workflows and data continuity between requests.

process.title: CAD add-on and user interface
items: CAD add-on and its user-facing UI.
Input submission from CAD to the backend API; server results displayed and applied in the CAD workflow.

process.title: Monitoring, testing, and iteration
items: Prometheus and Grafana in the server/monitoring stack.
Tested the integrated flow across CAD input, API, inference, storage, and CAD output.
Refined the workflow based on integration issues and model behaviour.

pipeline: Raw project data → inspection and EDA.
Cleaning, labelling, and dataset preparation (OpenCV where needed).
Model training and evaluation (PyTorch, YOLO; DETR experiments).
Model packaging and deployment behind the FastAPI backend.
Inference results → information extraction → structured API response → CAD add-on.

results: Progressed beyond model experimentation into an integrated CAD → server → CAD workflow with backend services, MySQL storage, and a CAD-side interface.
Measured detection metrics, latency, throughput, and workflow improvements will be added once approved for publication.
challenges: Integration: AI predictions had to become output usable inside a CAD application, not just a notebook result.
Service boundaries: processing and inference stay on the server so CAD acts as the user-facing client.
Data consistency: structured API responses and persistent records connect CAD input with downstream estimation.
Model selection: YOLO-based development and DETR experiments compared detection approaches.
Operational visibility: Prometheus and Grafana for monitoring the running stack.
